key_insight: Trajectory replay updates continuous-time generative models while retaining past tasks by learning a density-weighted mixture of historical and incoming velocity fields.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support continual updates to generative engineering models, but the abstract provides no solid-mechanics or constitutive-model validation.
method: Match frozen historical velocities along their trajectories and incoming-task velocities.
Balance retention and adaptation with a stability–plasticity coefficient.
Use mean velocity distillation to access historical trajectories with few network evaluations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over generative replay and distillation baselines on class-incremental image generation, plus preserved treatment-effect prediction in two biological case studies across two data modalities.
watch_item: Retention depends on the frozen historical model and the stability–plasticity balance; performance on mechanics data remains untested in the abstract.
paper_title: Trajectory Replay: Continuous-Time Mixture Transport for Lifelong Generative Models
